en: After her grandmother died, Nora never unpacked the last two boxes she had left behind.
At least that was what Nora had always told herself.

The boxes sat at the back of her apartment storage room beneath a broken floor lamp and three cartons of Christmas decorations. When she got home from the archives, she did not change clothes. She moved everything aside and dragged the first box into the living room.
MARA was written across the top.
Block capitals. Heavy strokes. As if she had been afraid time might erase the name.
Nora sat on the carpet and cut through the yellowed packing tape.
Old tax slips. Pediatric clinic receipts. Photographs. Letters from friends. A cheap scarf. A 1997 telephone directory.
She searched for forty minutes before she found a blue envelope containing two stiff paper tickets.
Nora stared at the age printed on the child's ticket.
She laid the tickets on the carpet and did not move for a long time.
All her life, people had told her that her mother left.
No one had told her that her mother had intended to take her.
Nora picked up her phone and called her great-aunt Ruth.
Old people could hear bad news in a badly timed phone call before a word was said.
"November twentieth, 1998. Rivermere to Edmonton. One adult, one child."
Nora switched the phone to her other hand.
The answer emptied Nora's mind of the next question.
She looked at the tickets on the floor.
"Then why did no one ever tell me?"
"Then I was six. Ten. Twenty. Thirty."
"Your grandmother thought there was no point."
"No point in telling me my mother was planning to take me with her?"
"She thought hope was worse than disappointment."
Nora kept the edge out of her voice by force.
"Why did Mara drop me at Grandma's on the nineteenth?"
"She wasn't employed by a company. She was a legal assistant at Mercer & Pike."
She had seen that name in the register that afternoon.
"When was the last time she called Grandma?"
"Your grandmother took the call. She told me about it later."
"That things were more complicated than she'd expected. She might be late. If she missed the morning train, she'd take one in the afternoon."
"But the next day someone signed for a document in person using her name."
Nothing came back through the line.
"An environmental liability addendum for Halden Urban Group."
"Did she have any connection to Halden?"
"Was Lena a friend of my mother's?"
Ruth did not answer for a long time.
"Lena Zhou died in a warehouse fire at Alder Yard on the nineteenth."
"And my mother disappeared the same night."
"Don't force two things together because they happened near each other."
Nora heard a cup being set down on the other end.
"Then start with the police from back then."
"A young officer came to the house."
"Martin... Martin Hale. I remember because your grandmother said he didn't look like a cop. Too skinny. Still had acne."
"About Mara's luggage. Her friends. The train tickets. Whether she might have left on her own."
"Because at the time we honestly thought she had."
"Your grandmother kept talking about a dark green coat."
"It wasn't Mara's. The police asked about it later. Apparently someone saw her that night wearing something like it."
"I don't know. Your grandmother complained that Mara was borrowing other people's clothes again."
"Why did she remember it so clearly?"
"She wasn't wearing it when she dropped you off. That much I'm sure of. Whenever she put it on, it was later."
zh: 外婆去世以后，诺拉一直没有整理她留下的最后两个纸箱。不是因为悲伤。
至少她一直这么告诉自己。
纸箱被放在公寓储物间最里面，上面压着一只坏掉的落地灯和三盒圣诞装饰。她回家以后没有换衣服，先搬开东西，把第一只箱子拖进客厅。
大写，粗重，一笔一画，像是怕时间把名字擦掉。诺拉坐在地毯上，用美工刀划开已经发黄的胶带。
旧税单、儿科诊所收据、一叠照片、几封朋友来信、一条廉价围巾，还有一本1997年的电话簿。她翻了四十分钟，直到在一只蓝色信封里找到两张硬纸票。Canadian Western Rail。
诺拉盯着儿童票上的年龄。
她把票放在地板上，很久没有动。
从小到大，所有人都告诉她，母亲离开了。没有人告诉她：母亲原本打算带她一起走。
她拿起电话，拨给姨婆露丝。
老人总能从不合时宜的电话里先听出坏消息。
“1998年11月20日，里弗米尔到埃德蒙顿。一张成人，一张儿童。”
诺拉把手机换到另一只手。
一句话，让诺拉突然不知道该继续问什么。
“后来我六岁、十岁、二十岁、三十岁。”
“没有必要让我知道我母亲原本打算带我走？”
诺拉压住声音里的锋利。
“她十九日晚上为什么把我送到外婆家？”
“她不是公司员工。她在Mercer & Pike做律师助理。”
她今天下午刚在登记册里看到这个名字。Mercer & Pike Legal。
“她最后一次给外婆打电话是什么时候？”
“大概七点前，六点五十分左右。”
“你外婆接的。她后来跟我说过。”
“玛拉说事情比想象中麻烦，她可能晚一点回来。如果赶不上早晨的车，就改下午。”
“可是第二天有人亲自用她的名字签收了一份文件。”
“Halden Urban Group的环境责任补充协议。”
“Lena Zhou在十九号晚上死在Alder Yard仓库。”
“我母亲也在十九号晚上失踪。”
老人声音突然严厉起来。
露丝那边传来一声杯子放下的轻响。
“Martin……Martin Hale。我记得，因为你外婆说他不像警察，太瘦，脸上还有青春痘。”
“玛拉的行李、朋友、票。还问她有没有可能自己离开。”
“因为那时候我们真的以为她走了。”
“还有一件事。你外婆后来一直念叨一件深绿色长外套。”
“不是她自己的。警方后来问过，我们才知道有人那晚见过她穿着类似的衣服。”
“我不知道。你外婆那时候还抱怨，说她又穿别人的衣服。”
“至少她把你送到外婆家时没穿。后来什么时候换上的，我们谁都不知道。”
